stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist is revising the pickup procedure. One prescription is for an ordinary Schedule VI drug that has not been designated by the Commissioner for the additional-drug identification requirement. Another is for a drug that has received that formal designation. Which statements correctly describe the Customer Identifier rule? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The designated additional drug is within the Customer Identifier rule even though it is not described as a Schedule II through V drug.
Every Schedule VI dispensing is within the rule because Massachusetts calls Schedule VI a controlled-substance schedule.
Dispensing a controlled substance in Schedule II, III, IV, or V is within the rule's stated scope.
The ordinary Schedule VI drug is not brought within the rule merely by its Schedule VI classification.
A familiar customer may receive a covered drug without identification or the documented hardship procedure.

explanation.core_reasoning: 247 CMR 9.04(14) applies the Customer Identifier requirement when a licensee dispenses a controlled substance in Schedules II through V or an additional drug formally designated under the cited Department regulation. It does not automatically cover every Massachusetts Schedule VI drug. A designated additional drug is covered by the designation, while an ordinary, undesignated Schedule VI drug is not covered merely because Massachusetts places prescription drugs in Schedule VI. Familiarity with the customer is not an independent exception.

choice_analysis.A: Correct: formal additional-drug designation is an independent route into the rule's scope.
choice_analysis.B: The regulation enumerates Schedules II through V and designated additional drugs, not Schedule VI as a whole.
choice_analysis.C: Correct: Schedule II through V dispensing is expressly within the rule.
choice_analysis.D: Correct: Schedule VI classification alone does not satisfy either enumerated route.
choice_analysis.E: Familiarity does not replace identification or, when serious hardship exists, the complete documentation, printed-information, and signature procedure.

related_facts: The Customer Identifier is obtained by inspecting valid government-issued identification of the ultimate user or agent
A serious-hardship dispensing requires both pharmacy documentation and recipient-entered identifying information and signature
explanation.mpje_trap: Massachusetts uses the term Schedule VI broadly, but this identification rule deliberately names Schedules II through V and a separate designation pathway.

reasoning_steps: Identify the two routes that place a dispensing within the Customer Identifier rule
Compare the ordinary Schedule VI drug with the formally designated additional drug
Reject familiarity as a substitute for the specified hardship procedure
